answer: Because the kernel cliff is fixed at deposit and logged in the comet ledger, the lantern audit publishes how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 20 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. That is 32 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
